subject: Update on an old (?) problem: Centering labels

messages.author: 20a857807016d58a
messages.subject: Update on an old (?) problem: Centering labels
parts:
Dear expeRts,

I am a new user of ggplot2 and I am wondering if there is an update on
the following problem:
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/86e6e831b149db/6c5419340d308e34?lnk=gst&q=label+center#6c5419340d308e34
I would like to "center" the title and the x-axis label according to
the gray background, not the whole width of the plot. Is this
possible?
(it is highly advised from a typography perspective).

Cheers and thanks,

Marius

messages.author: 439a20c9d67ff394
messages.subject: Re: Update on an old (?) problem: Centering labels
parts:
This popped more recently (just a month or two ago) than the link you
found, here:

http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/7eef88dc47e17bba/8027f0e6b7f5fd0f?lnk=gst&q=center+axis+label#8027f0e6b7f5fd0f

and as of then it didn't sound like an "official" fix existed. The
thread you linked to has some code of Baptiste's that, while still a
bit opaque to me, was enough for me to hack this together, which has
been working for me:

adjLabel <- function(xlabel, xAxisCex = 0.8,adj=0.59){
x <- xlabel[which.max(nchar(xlabel))]
offset <- grobWidth(textGrob(lab=x,gp=gpar(cex=xAxisCex)))
rs <- c(convertUnit(offset,"npc"))
rs <- rs * adj
return(c(unit(0.5,"npc")) + rs)
}


yVals <- unlist(lapply(sample(1:26,10),
FUN=function(x){
paste(sample(letters,x),collapse="")}))
dat <- data.frame(x=runif(10),y=yVals)

ggplot(dat,aes(x=x,y=y)) +
geom_point() +
labs(x="Label To Center",y=NULL) +
opts(axis.title.x=theme_text(hjust=adjLabel(dat$y)))

Why 0.59? No idea. I'm sure it's because I'm doing something wrong, or
something. But it's producing centered axis titles for me, so (at the
moment) I'm happy. Perhaps this hack will prompt some more
knowledgable folks to chime in with something more elegant/
understandable.

messages.author: 20a857807016d58a
messages.subject: Re: Update on an old (?) problem: Centering labels
parts:
Hi Joran,

Thanks for your help. After working with your code I realized that the
position x-label position changes with the random numbers to be
plotted. If you play with the seed you'll find examples where the
label is not properly centered with respect to the gray background.
Can you build a minimal example with the "manual" solution you
suggested at the end of the recent post? At the moment, it's probably
the simplest way to adjust both labels and the title.

Cheers,

Marius


library(ggplot2)

set.seed(100)

adjLabel <- function(xlabel, xAxisCex=0.8, adj=0.59){

x <- xlabel[which.max(nchar(xlabel))]
offset <- grobWidth(textGrob(lab=x,gp=gpar(cex=xAxisCex)))
rs <- c(convertUnit(offset,"npc"))
rs <- rs * adj
return(c(unit(0.5,"npc")) + rs)
}

yVals <- unlist(lapply(sample(1:26,10),
FUN=function(x){
paste(sample(letters,x),collapse="")}))
dat <- data.frame(x=runif(10),y=yVals)
ggplot(dat, aes(x=x, y=y)) +

geom_point() +
labs(x="Label To Center", y=NULL) +
opts(axis.title.x=theme_text(hjust=adjLabel(dat$y)))

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Update on an old (?) problem: Centering labels
parts:
Hi,

You can probably use grid to edit the position of the label, though
admittedly it's rather painful.


(p <- qplot(1,"aaaaaaaaa", col="blue") + xlab(expression("this is
"*alpha*" x title")))

g <- ggplotGrob(p)

gg <- getGrob(g,"axis.title.y.text",grep=TRUE)
ytitle <- if(is.zero(gg) || is.null(gg)) ggplot2:::.zeroGrob else
editGrob(gg, vp=NULL)

gg <- getGrob(g,"axis.text.y.text",grep=TRUE)
ylabel <- if(is.zero(gg) || is.null(gg)) ggplot2:::.zeroGrob else
editGrob(gg, vp=NULL)

xtitle <- getGrob(g,"axis.title.x.text",grep=TRUE)

grid.remove("axis.title.x.text",grep=TRUE)

seekViewport("xlabel")
vp <- viewport(x=unit(1, "npc"),
width=unit(1,"npc") - grobWidth(ytitle) - grobWidth(ylabel),
just="right")
grid.rect(vp=vp, gp=gpar(lty=2))
grid.text(xtitle$label, vp=vp)


HTH,

baptiste

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Update on an old (?) problem: Centering labels
parts:
Hi:

Kohske, this is really useful. In fact, it doesn't just affect
alignment in one direction, it also deals with a problem that has come
up often on this list: separation of the axis titles from the axis
ticks. Here's a little example to illustrate what I mean:

# Generate some fake regression data with three groups:
xx <- rpois(60, 10)
df <- data.frame(gp = factor(rep(c('Group I', 'Group II', 'Group
III'), each = 20)),
x = xx,
y = rep(c(2, 4, 6), each = 20) + 3 * xx + rnorm(60, s = 3))

# Do a simple scatterplot with fitted LS lines per group, color coded by group.
# I wanted a legend here because that's usually what causes the text alignment
# problems.
g <- ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = gp))
g + geom_point(size = 2.5) +
geom_smooth(method = 'lm', size = 1, se = FALSE) +
labs(x = 'This is my x label', y = 'This is my y label') +
opts(title = 'This is the main title')

# Run these one at a time and observe what happens to the 'outward' spacing
# as well as the intended shift in direction:
grid.edit('axis.title.x', grep = TRUE, x = unit(0.52, 'npc'), y =
unit(0, 'npc'))
grid.edit('axis.title.y', grep = TRUE, x = unit(0, 'npc'), y =
unit(0.53, 'npc'))
grid.edit('plot.title', grep = TRUE, x = unit(0.52, 'npc'), y =
unit(0.7, 'npc'))

Just for fun, try out the main plot with y = unit(0, 'npc') and then
play with some alternatives.

It's enough to make one want to learn grid graphics :) Thanks for the
tip, and hope this is of some help to others.

Dennis

Dear Kohske, Dear Dennis,

many thanks, that looks nice.
I had to fine-tune some parameters to center the labels / title. On
doing so, I wanted to have more space between the x-axis and its label
(see below). Do you know how I can make the label fully visible again?
If the distance between the axis and the label is too large, the label
does not show up in the plot anymore. I tried to work with push/
popViewport but I couldn't manage to get this to work.

Cheers,

Marius


library(ggplot2)

z <- 2:10
df <- data.frame(x=z, y=z)

g <- qplot(x, y, data=df)
g + labs(x = 'x', y = 'x') +
opts(title = 'x')

grid.edit('axis.title.x', grep = TRUE, x = unit(0.513, 'npc'), y =
unit(-0.4, 'npc'))
grid.edit('axis.title.y', grep = TRUE, x = unit(-0.2, 'npc'), y =
unit(0.517, 'npc'))
grid.edit('plot.title', grep = TRUE, x = unit(0.513, 'npc'), y =
unit(1, 'npc'))

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Update on an old (?) problem: Centering labels
parts:
Hi,

Shifting the label by hand is always going to be a rather fragile
procedure since the misalignment depends crucially on the the y-axis
labels (hence, changing the data of the plot or the scale may break
the manual alignment).

I've wrapped the code i proposed earlier in a function that should
work for basic plots (one panel, no fancy options, etc.). The example
becomes,

p <- qplot(1,"aaaaaaaaa", col="blue") + xlab(expression("this is to
become a centered x title"))

source("http://ggextra.googlecode.com/svn/trunk/inst/tests/label-fix.r")
fix.label(p, vjust=1)

HTH,

baptiste

Concerning my last question, I found a hint in a recent post of Dennis

71c124572d005d1f/7c68f5011ed80090?
lnk=gst&q=viewport#7c68f5011ed80090). I'm not a grid expert, so if the

Marius



library(ggplot2)

z <- 2:10
df <- data.frame(x=z, y=z)

g <- qplot(x, y, data=df) + labs(x = 'x', y = 'x') + opts(title = 'x')

grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport())
myviewport <- viewport(width=0.8, height=0.8, x=0.5, y=0.5)
print(g, vp=myviewport)
